- One-line enhancement description (can be used as a release note): Add a KEP for the Work API https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/work-api under `keps/sig-multicluster`, bringing the 2021 design proposal up to date with the API as it exists today (including `AppliedWork`) so it is documented, tracked, and evolved through the same process as the other SIG-Multicluster APIs. - Kubernetes Enhancement Proposal: - Discussion Link: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/work-api/blob/master/docs/proposals/20210219-work-api.md - PRs by stage and milestone: - [x] Alpha - v1.xx - [x] KEP (`k/enhancements`) update PR(s): https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/6457 - [x] Code (`k/k`) update PR(s): https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/work-api - [x] Docs (`k/website`) update PR(s): https://multicluster.sigs.k8s.io/concepts/work-api/
<!-- Uncomment these as you prepare the enhancement for the next stage - [ ] Beta - v1.xx - [ ] KEP (`k/enhancements`) update PR(s): - [ ] Code (`k/k`) update PR(s): - [ ] Docs (`k/website`) update(s): - [ ] Stable - v1.xx - [ ] KEP (`k/enhancements`) update PR(s): - [ ] Code (`k/k`) update PR(s): - [ ] Docs (`k/website`) update(s): -->
The Work API was accepted by SIG-Multicluster in 2021 and is implemented in https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/work-api, but the design has been updated. For example, the `AppliedWork` which has been discussed and agreed upon in the SIG-MC community https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/work-api/pull/14/changes and https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/work-api/pull/29 in 2023.
Every other SIG-MC APIs has its KEP created and maintained. The Work API is the one exception, which means there is no path to link to and no normal place to land design updates.
This Work KEP would migrate the original proposal into the KEP template, reconcile it with the current API and implementation. **It is not proposing changes to the API itself.**

entry.title: SLM: Coordinate Node lifecycle condition writers
entry.summary:
### Enhancement Description [Node lifecycle conditions](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/node/node-lifecycle-conditions/) provide a shared place to publish important lifecycle state, but the Condition API does not provide coordination semantics. Multiple actors, like admins running `kubectl drain`, remediation controllers, Node Problem Detector, infrastructure operators, ect., can all observe the same Node and independently decide to write lifecycle state invalidating each other.
The issue is Node Conditions writes are unaware of one another, so they can overwrite another actor's lifecycle signal or trigger conflicting remediation. There isn't an available way to coordinate who set the condition, how long it will be set for, ect..
This KEP will define a coordination mechanism for Node lifecycle condition writers and a way to discover ownership. The mechanism should allow an actor to declare that it is managing a Node lifecycle operation, identify the scope of that ownership, and give other writers and readers enough structured context to avoid conflicting updates. It will also define how readers should interpret lifecycle state when an owner is present.
- One-line enhancement description (can be used as a release note): Add coordination mechanism for actors writing Node lifecycle conditions. - Kubernetes Enhancement Proposal: TBD - Discussion Link: - Use cases doc: [Node Lifecycle Coordination Using Conditions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/12nMG9Yyzd5D8iams5Oc4BEtfupe-li-Kxsxm_G7D_Ts/edit?usp=sharing) - [KEP-5683: Node Lifecycle Conditions](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/5683-lifecycle-conditions) - [Specialized Lifecycle Management](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5683) - [SLM: Publish kubectl drain state as Node conditions](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/6251) - [kubernetes/node-problem-detector#1176](https://github.com/kubernetes/node-problem-detector/issues/1176) - [kubernetes/node-problem-detector#457](https://github.com/kubernetes/node-problem-detector/issues/457) - PRs by stage and milestone: - [ ] Alpha - TBD - [ ] KEP (`k/enhancements`) update PR(s): - [ ] Code (`k/k`) update PR(s): - [ ] Docs (`k/website`) update PR(s):

entry.title: PodGroup runtime satisfaction condition
entry.summary:
### Enhancement Description
- One-line enhancement description (can be used as a release note): Add a `PodGroupSatisfied` condition to PodGroup status, reporting whether a gang currently has at least `minCount` scheduled members. - Kubernetes Enhancement Proposal: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/6414 - Discussion Link: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136334 - PRs by stage and milestone: - [ ] Alpha - v1.39 - [ ] KEP (`k/enhancements`) update PR(s): https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/6414 - [ ] Code (`k/k`) update PR(s): - [ ] Docs (`k/website`) update PR(s):
`PodGroupInitiallyScheduled` is terminal by design, so a gang that has dropped below `minCount` looks the same in status as a healthy one. Consumers re-derive group health from member pods instead: LeaderWorkerSet infers it from Pod phase, which is ambiguous under gang scheduling (kubernetes-sigs/lws#1056); the multi-pod PDB KEP (#5671) recomputes `healthy_pods >= minCount` in the eviction path; JobSet defers the question entirely.
This adds one condition, computed from the per-group member state the scheduler cache already maintains. No schema change and no scheduling behavior change; the feature gate `PodGroupRuntimeSatisfaction` is kube-scheduler only.
Whether a gang owner can choose how replacement members are admitted after initial placement is out of scope, and is recorded as future work in the KEP.
_Please keep this description up to date. This will help the Enhancement Team to track the evolution of the enhancement efficiently._
/sig scheduling

entry.title: DRA Extended Resource Capacity
entry.summary:
## Enhancement Description
**One-line enhancement description (can be used as a release note):** Cluster administrators can declare a fixed device capacity request (for example, a number of GPU time-slicing shares) on a `DeviceClass`, so that the scheduler applies it automatically to every `ResourceClaim` it synthesizes to satisfy that class's extended resource requests.
**Kubernetes Enhancement Proposal:** https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/6408
**Discussion Link:**
**Primary contact (assignee):** @shivamerla
**Responsible SIGs:** SIG Scheduling, SIG Node
**Enhancement target (which target equals to which milestone):**
- Alpha release target (x.y): 1.38 - Beta release target (x.y): TBD - Stable release target (x.y): TBD
**Please keep this description up to date. This will help the Enhancement Team to track the evolution of the enhancement efficiently.**
## Enhancement Goal
[DRA Extended Resource](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-scheduling/5004-dra-extended-resource) (GA in 1.37) lets a `DeviceClass` declare an `extendedResourceName` so classic `resources.requests`/`resources.limits` entries (e.g. `nvidia.com/gpu: 1`) are satisfied by DRA devices, with the scheduler synthesizing a `ResourceClaim` on the pod's behalf. [DRA Consumable Capacity](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-scheduling/5075-dra-consumable-capacity) (Beta in 1.36) lets a `ResourceClaim`'s device request specify a `capacity.requests` map so a shareable device (`allowMultipleAllocations: true`) is only partially consumed, instead of being handed out as a whole device.
Today there is no way to use consumable capacity for extended resources: the extended-resource-synthesized `ResourceClaim`'s device request never sets `Capacity`, so extended resources can only ever request whole, exclusively-allocated devices. There is no way for `nvidia.com/gpu.shared: 1` (the classic device-plugin-era resource name used for GPU time-slicing) to end up as "give me 2 shares of a shareable GPU" through DRA.
This enhancement adds an optional `extendedResourceCapacityRequests` field to `DeviceClassSpec`. When set, the scheduler copies it onto the `Capacity` field of every `ExactDeviceRequest` it synthesizes for that class's `ExtendedResourceName`, using the exact same `CapacityRequirements` type and per-allocation semantics `DeviceRequest.Capacity` already has. This is deliberately a thin, additive KEP: no new allocation semantics, no new scheduler algorithm, just wiring an existing field through an existing synthesis path.
**Primary motivating use case:** DRA Driver for NVIDIA GPUs already lets an administrator advertise a fixed number of `"shares"` per GPU (`--consumable-shares=<N>`, via `DRAConsumableCapacity`). Today, migrating a workload from device-plugin time-slicing (`nvidia.com/gpu.shared: 1`) to this DRA-based sharing model requires the workload to switch to a `ResourceClaim`/`ResourceClaimTemplate`. With this enhancement, an administrator can instead publish one `DeviceClass` per desired slice size (e.g. `extendedResourceName: nvidia.com/gpu.shared` with `extendedResourceCapacityRequests: {requests: {shares: "1"}}`), and existing pod specs using the classic extended resource syntax get routed to a correctly-sized GPU slice with zero pod-spec changes. The mechanism itself is generic and applies to any DRA driver/capacity name (NIC bandwidth slices etc.), not just GPUs.
